memos.headline: AAPL and MSFT Lead on Relative Strength; CAT and UNH Show Deteriorating Trends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL is the standout leader—just 1.2% off its 52-week high, +8.1% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, RSI 64 with room to run, and sitting 17.4% above its 200-day mean, confirming a powerful uptrend. MSFT's 12-week relative strength of +31.2% vs SPY is extraordinary, though its RSI at 53 and 8.9% drawdown suggest it's digesting gains rather than breaking out fresh. On the other side, CAT is the weakest name in the group: down 18.6% over 12 weeks, 24% off its 52-week high, and showing -22.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—this is a broken trend I want no part of until it reclaims its 50-day mean. UNH is similarly concerning with RSI at 36.9, 6.8% below its 50-day mean, and -11% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks, signaling institutional distribution.

views.note: Dominant relative strength (+8.1% vs SPY 4w, +10.8% 12w), only 1.2% from 52w high with RSI 64—trend intact; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~$320).
Massive 12w relative strength of +31.2% vs SPY and well above both moving averages, but 8.9% drawdown and modest RSI 53 suggest consolidation; a break below ~$465 (50d area) would change my view.
Healthy uptrend with +12% above 200d mean and positive relative strength, but only 5.7% from highs with middling RSI 54—trend-following long but not high conviction; watch $214 (50d area) as support.
Down 18.6% over 12 weeks, 24% off 52w high, and -22.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—this is a clear downtrend; would reconsider only on a sustained move back above the 50-day mean (~$840).
RSI 36.9 is near oversold, 6.8% below 50d mean, -11% relative strength vs SPY over 12w—classic distribution pattern; need to see RSI recover above 50 and price reclaim $405 before reconsidering.
Sitting right at its 50d mean with RSI 48 and -2.3% relative strength vs SPY over 4w—neither trending nor breaking down; a close below $248 (200d area ~$240) would turn me negative.
Flat relative to both 50d and 200d means, 12.4% off highs, negative 12w returns—no trend to follow here; low vol (ATR 1.6%) limits downside but also upside.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Deliver Extraordinary Earnings Power; XOM and PG Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer disparity in earnings trajectories across this universe. NVDA posted $96.2B in quarterly revenue (+105.9% YoY) with a 62.0% net margin, while GOOGL printed a remarkable 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue—both reflecting durable, high-quality earnings growth that I want to own. On the other end, XOM's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to just 4.9%, and PG saw net income decline 15.8% on anemic 1.5% top-line growth, exactly the cash-flow compression profile I refuse to pay for. AMZN's 244.9% net income growth and 31.2% margin expansion are impressive but the $133B debt load warrants monitoring; CAT's 24% revenue growth and 17.5% margin are encouraging for a cyclical but sustainability is the key question. I would revisit my XOM and PG avoidance if XOM's Q2 margin recovers above 8% or PG demonstrates positive net income growth in the next quarter.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY with 62% net margin on $33B debt is exceptional earnings power; would reassess if margins compress below 50%.
93.7% net margin and 24.2% revenue growth on minimal $14.8B debt is the cleanest balance sheet and highest-quality earnings in the universe.
39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, and 31.3% net income growth on moderate $40.3B debt reflect durable, compounding earnings.
Net income surged 244.9% YoY to $62.7B with margin expanding to 31.2%, but $133B total debt tempers my conviction—watching leverage trajectory closely.
24% revenue growth and 64.9% earnings growth are strong but cyclicality risk is high; need to see sustained margins above 15% before getting constructive.
41.2% net income growth and 36.9% margin are solid for a bank, but $460.5B debt and rate-cycle sensitivity keep me neutral.
16.4% revenue growth reaccelerating with 27.2% net margin and 27.1% earnings growth is healthy, though $82.3B debt is worth monitoring.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with only 4.9% net margin despite 61% earnings recovery; need to see top-line reacceleration.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin is textbook cash-flow compression; would reconsider if Q2 margin recovers above 8%.
Net income declining 15.8% on just 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% margin signals deteriorating earnings power in a defensive name.

memos.headline: Fed Pauses at 4% but Sticky 3.4% CPI and 5% 10y Yields Signal a Hawkish-Hold Regime That Punishes Duration and Favors Defensives
memos.body: I see a clear hawkish-pause regime: the Fed hiked the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, yet the effective rate has been flat at 3.63%, suggesting the hike was recent and the committee is now on hold with inflation still running 3.4% YoY on the August CPI print. The labor market remains firm at 4.1% unemployment (down 20bp over both 3m and 12m horizons), giving the Fed no urgency to ease. The 10y yield at 5.01%—up 90bp over the past year and 55bp in just three months—is repricing term premium aggressively, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed to just 27bp, flattening 27bp YoY, consistent with markets pricing higher-for-longer policy rates. In this environment I favor short-duration, cash-generative names and banks that benefit from elevated rate levels, while avoiding long-duration growth equities whose valuations are most sensitive to a 5% discount rate. A CPI print breaking below 3% or unemployment rising above 4.5% would flip my regime call toward easing expectations.

views.note: Banks benefit from a hawkish-hold regime with a positively sloped curve (27bp 10y-2y) and elevated absolute rate levels supporting net interest margins.
Energy is a short-duration, real-asset sector that hedges sticky 3.4% inflation and is less sensitive to the 5% 10y yield environment.
Staples offer defensive positioning but their bond-proxy characteristics face headwinds from the 90bp YoY surge in the 10y yield to 5.01%.
High-multiple growth names face the most valuation compression as the 10y yield breaches 5% and the Fed shows no inclination to ease.
Strong cash generation provides some buffer, but consumer hardware demand and the elevated discount rate at 5% 10y keep me from getting constructive.
Recurring revenue is a positive, but duration sensitivity at a 5% 10y yield and no near-term easing catalyst limit upside.
Consumer cyclical exposure plus long-duration cloud capex story is poorly positioned in a 3.4% CPI / 5% 10y yield regime.
Ad revenue is cyclically resilient and the multiple is more moderate than peers, but the macro backdrop offers no tailwind.
Firm labor market supports capex but the flattening curve and rising long rates historically weigh on industrial multiples.
Defensive healthcare cash flows and pricing power in a 3.4% inflation environment make UNH relatively attractive versus duration-sensitive growth.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT and AMZN Surged on Results While AAPL Sold Off Hard — Crowded Positive Tone Risk in Tech Winners
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across the universe. MSFT (+15.5%) and AMZN (+15.3%) both posted massive positive reactions to their late-July results, and NVDA followed with +8.7% on its August report — these three names now carry crowded positive sentiment that may already be priced after nearly two months of digestion. AAPL stands out negatively with a -7.4% post-earnings drop and a subsequent board-level change (8-K/A on 9/1), suggesting a narrative shift that could still have room to worsen. CAT's +5.6% earnings pop and a new material agreement filed 9/1 point to a quieter but constructive tone in industrials that has attracted less attention. PG's mild -1.9% reaction alongside multiple Reg FD and officer-change filings on the same day reads as neutral-to-slightly-negative, with no clear catalyst to reverse sentiment near-term.

views.note: Negative earnings reaction of -7.4% followed by a director/officer change suggests deteriorating narrative with further downside risk.
The +15.5% earnings pop was enormous but nearly two months old; positive sentiment is likely fully priced and I see crowding risk.
Similar to MSFT, the +15.3% post-earnings surge is well-digested; recent officer change and other-events filings add noise but no clear new positive catalyst.
Strong +8.7% earnings reaction is more recent (late August) but new debt agreement and vague 'Other Events' filing cloud the picture; positive tone may be peaking.
Solid +5.6% earnings reaction with less crowded sentiment, and a new material agreement suggests constructive fundamental momentum under the radar.
Mild -1.9% earnings reaction and multiple same-day filings including officer changes suggest stable but uninspiring sentiment with no clear directional edge.
Only a Reg FD disclosure on 9/8 with no earnings reaction data available; insufficient signal to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Surging Oil and Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Stress; NVDA and XOM Most Exposed
memos.body: I am flagging a sharp divergence between the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which has doubled in a month to 354, and the VIX at a relatively benign 15.44—credit spreads at 2.70% HY OAS are similarly complacent. WTI crude at $103.21, up 28% over three months and 20% in the last month alone, points to a supply-side disruption consistent with energy-security or sanctions-related stress, not demand-driven strength given the flattening yield curve (10y-2y spread collapsed 26bp in a month to just 0.27pp). NVDA has filed two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3), which in the current environment I read as likely related to export-control or China-policy developments—this is the name most structurally exposed to tightening semiconductor restrictions. XOM is the clearest beneficiary of the oil spike, while CAT faces a mixed picture: infrastructure demand is supportive but elevated policy uncertainty and potential sanctions-related supply-chain disruptions cloud the outlook. I would change my view on NVDA if we see a concrete easing of chip export controls, and on XOM if OPEC+ signals a meaningful production increase or sanctions are relaxed.

views.note: Two 8-Ks in three weeks amid surging policy uncertainty (354, +130% m/m) strongly suggest export-control headwinds; structurally most exposed to China semiconductor restrictions.
WTI at $103.21 (+28% 3m) on what appears to be supply-side/geopolitical disruption directly benefits XOM's upstream margins.
Infrastructure tailwinds persist but policy uncertainty doubling in a month and potential sanctions-related supply-chain risks limit conviction.
China supply-chain concentration remains a structural risk given elevated policy uncertainty, but no specific 8-K filings suggest imminent disruption.
Cloud/enterprise software is relatively insulated from energy and trade-policy shocks; Sep 2 Reg FD filing suggests proactive investor communication rather than distress.
Domestic healthcare is largely shielded from trade/energy geopolitics, but the Sep 8 Reg FD disclosure amid surging policy uncertainty warrants monitoring for regulatory risk.
